text:
liam: Heads up — A/B rollout (traffic split 50/50) for release/0.69 is showing a p99 latency regression on cohort B (~+18% vs baseline) and KV cache miss rate ~2x. CI bench64 also failed earlier on the same commit. Should we pause the rollout/gate auto-revert? @yasmin @emma :eyes:
perf-bot: bench64 CI failure at commit abc123... def456 -> p95 +12%, p99 +20%. See: https://ci.internal/bench/abc123 :robot_face:
emma: I pulled traces from a few requests. Preliminary root cause looks like kernel-selector now prefers tiled kernel for short sequences when batching window is larger. That kernel has slightly worse small-batch latency and its memory access pattern is nudging the KV cache eviction curve higher. Also batching heuristic change bumped typical batch size up ~1.6x which increases KV churn.
raj: hmm — so two levers: kernel selection policy and batching window. Can we quickly force the previous kernel hint for the rollout cohort while we bisect?
liam: yes. We can set ENV KERNEL_HINT=preferred_small for the B cohort. Quick test on a small pool reduced p99 back to baseline in my local replay.
yasmin: please pause A/B while we confirm. I'll flip the rollout to 10/90 and pause further propagation. Opening a tracking thread in incidents. :lock:
emma: also worth noting the CI perf test exercises a long prefix case which stresses KV lifetime; that amplified the regression signal. I ran a short profile and pasted the hot stack:```
# simplified
compute_kernel_selector() +8ms
execute_tiled_kernel() +18ms
kv_cache_evict_loop() +12ms
```
liam: proposal: add temporary canary guard that pauses cohort if ANY of: p99 > 1.12x baseline, kv_miss_rate > 1.5x baseline, or tokens/sec per-GPU drops > 10%. If triggered, auto-scale traffic back to baseline and create a rollback candidate. Thoughts?
raj: +1 on the guard thresholds, but make them configurable per-model (long seqs vs short). Need to avoid noisy pauses for heavy-tail workloads.
emma: agree, and add an immediate mitigation: set batching.window_ms=4 for cohort B (from 8) which should lower batch size and reduce KV churn. Also push a kernel-hint override. That buys time for the bisect.
liam: I can run a targeted bisect across commits abc100..abc123 to find the first commit that flips kernel preference. I'll run the kernel-only bisect script:```
./tools/perf-bisect --range abc100..abc123 --test bench64 --kernel-hint "none" --replay modelX
```
raj: if bisect points to the batching heuristic change, we should revert that and re-roll with smaller window and additional telemetry. If it points to kernel selector logic, revert the selector change and add a fallback blacklist for the tiled kernel on <64 tokens.
yasmin: please coordinate the rollback plan and post the immediate actions here. I'll notify platform teams and hold the rollout.
liam: immediate actions I did: 1) reduced cohort B traffic to 10% at 1829998890 2) applied KERNEL_HINT=preferred_small for cohort B 3) set batching.window_ms=4 for cohort B. Early telemetry shows p99 down ~9% from the spike.
rollout-bot: Rollout modified: cohort B traffic -> 10% (user: yasmin). Env overrides applied to cohort B. Auto-redeploy started.
emma: next: liam please run the bisect and paste the candidate commit. If it's a perf regression only in certain models we might ship a narrow revert or kernel hint flag instead of full revert.
liam: running bisect now, ETA ~25m. I'll post results and suggested revert commits.
raj: also log a perf regression ticket and attach the profiling artifacts (perf traces, kv miss histograms). We should add a canary SLO gate in the rollout system: automatic pause + run perf-bisect job when threshold exceeded.
emma: agree — let's make the gate run a lightweight replay and only auto-revert if the replay confirms regression. Otherwise pause for manual triage.
yasmin: thanks all. I'll keep the rollout on hold until we have a bisect result and a clear revert plan. :thumbsup:
